metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent demonstrated ability to create message filters in Thunderbird. This compositional variant chains two filter objectives: forwarding and mark-as-read, both within demonstrated capability.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can create multiple message filters; set forward action; set mark-as-read action from the action dropdown (visible in screenshot 5)
metadata.explanation: Getter reads all filter actions from msgFilterRules.dat. Metric awards 0.5 for a forward filter targeting anonym-x2024@gmail.com, and 0.5 for any filter with mark-as-read action. Scoring is additive with partial credit for each objective. llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads msgFilterRules.dat from the Thunderbird profile to extract filter state — the right approach for verifying Thunderbird message filters.
Getter detects both required filter types: forward action (via 'forward' in action value + actionValue line) and mark-as-read action (via 'mark' and 'read' in action value).

Metric correctly handles expected parameter: since expected.type='rule', the framework passes config['rules']={'forward_to': 'anonym-x2024@gmail.com'} directly; metric accesses expected.get('forward_to') correctly.
Both instruction requirements are verified: 0.5 credit for forward filter targeting anonym-x2024@gmail.com, 0.5 credit for mark-as-read filter — matching the two-objective task structure.
Postconfig closes Thunderbird before evaluation, which is appropriate since verification reads filesystem files (msgFilterRules.dat) rather than UI state.

Minor concern: getter reads all msgFilterRules.dat files without filtering by account (anonym-x2024@outlook.com). In practice this is not an issue given the single-account Thunderbird profile used in setup.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional: scope the msgFilterRules.dat search to the specific account directory containing 'outlook' or 'anonym-x2024' to guard against false positives if other accounts exist in the profile.
